svg.text: virtio_net / page_pool: one RX page reaches two skbs while page_pool counts one reference
ddm-pcache fix-history #23. Measured with a per-pfn owner table that records which skb installed each page_pool page into a frag array.
CORRECT LIFECYCLE — the allocation's single reference IS the skb's
1. page_pool hands out page P
try_fill_recv() -> page_pool_alloc_va() -> __page_pool_alloc_netmems_slow()
pp_ref_count(P) = 1 page _refcount = 1
2. posted to the receive virtqueue
add_recvbuf_mergeable() -> virtnet_rq_submit() -> virtqueue_add_inbuf_ctx()
3. returned by the device, one packet's buffer chain
receive_mergeable() -> virtnet_rq_get_buf() -> virtqueue_get_buf_ctx()
4. installed into skb A's frag array — NO reference taken
__skb_fill_netmem_desc() "Does not take any additional reference"
skb A frag[i] -> P pp_ref_count(P) still 1 (it is A's)
5. skb A released — P goes back to the pool, not to the buddy
skb_release_data() -> __skb_frag_unref() -> napi_pp_put_page()
pp_ref_count 1 -> 0 => recycled into pool->alloc.cache / ptr_ring
P is reusable, still owned by the pool. This is the steady state.
WHAT THE DUMPS SHOW — P is handed out again while skb A still holds it
1-4. same as the left: P installed into skb A frag[i]
pp_ref_count(P) = 1 skb A owns that one reference
5. THE DEFECT — page_pool hands P out a second time
P is handed out as a fresh buffer while skb A's frag still points at it.
pp_ref_count(P) is STILL 1 — the second hand-out took no reference
The pool's own cache and ptr_ring show no duplicate entry at crash time.
6. posted and returned again — the virtqueue stays balanced
measured for the offending page: posts=1889 gets=1889 outstanding=0
So it is NOT a double post, and NOT the same token returned twice.
7. installed into skb B frag[j] — two owners, one reference
__skb_fill_netmem_desc() again — again taking no reference
skb A frag[i] -> P and skb B frag[j] -> P pp_ref_count = 1
8. skb A released — P is freed to the BUDDY ALLOCATOR
napi_pp_put_page() -> pp_ref 1->0 -> page_pool_return_page()
-> __free_frozen_pages() page _refcount = 0, PP_SIGNATURE cleared
P now belongs to nobody. skb B's frag[j] is a dangling pointer.
9. skb B released 24 us later — BUG
skb_defer_free_flush() -> napi_consume_skb() -> skb_release_data()
VM_BUG_ON_PAGE(page_ref_count(page) == 0)
kernel BUG at ./include/linux/mm.h RIP: skb_release_data+0x...
diverges here
What the per-pfn owner probe recorded (four reproductions, 7.3.0-rc3+)
PP_OWNER: pfn 0x10bf82 has refcount 0 while skb ffff888106716000 frag 15 still points at it
PP_OWNER: installer[0] skb=0000888106717100 cpu=7 from receive_mergeable+0x153 [virtio_net]
PP_OWNER: installer[1] skb=0000888104782000 cpu=7 from receive_mergeable+0x153 [virtio_net]
PP_OWNER: virtqueue posts=1889 gets=1889 outstanding=0
PP_OWNER: totals: posts=12159356 gets=12158862 dropped=0
Two different skbs, and the crashing skb is a third one — the page was installed at least three times.
The per-page post/get counts are equal, which is what moves the fault off the virtqueue and onto the pool.
Earlier dumps show the same shape inside a single skb (frag 4 and frag 9, or frag 0 and frag 2).
The installing code differs every time — installers are victims
pfn 0x16b3eb page_to_skb + virtnet_skb_append_frag
frag[0] off=26 len=4070 frag[2] off=0 len=4096
pfn 0x10a0bd virtnet_skb_append_frag, twice
frag[3] off=0 len=4096 frag[8] off=0 len=4096
pfn 0x13c092 tcp_try_coalesce, twice
frag[6] off=0 len=4096 frag[8] off=0 len=822
Three unrelated paths, each doing the ordinary thing with a page it
was handed. Their only common factor is the page arriving twice.
off=26 is 12 (virtio hdr) + 14 (eth hdr): page_to_skb took its copy path.
Ruled out by instrumentation that stayed silent while the BUG fired
- a buffer posted to the virtqueue twice (probe v1, and posts==gets)
- the virtqueue returning a token that was never posted
- receive_mergeable()'s err_skb / mergeable_buf_free() error paths
- the same data buffer released twice in place
- the same skb released twice, or queued twice for deferred free
- GRO (reproduces with gro off; note tcp_try_coalesce runs anyway)
- the page_type change db359fccf212 (its revert is already in 7.3-rc3)
Caution: per-packet instrumentation suppresses the reproduction, so a
silent probe is only evidence if the BUG fired in that same run.
